headline: Missouri Governor Kehoe Taps DNR Director Kurt Schaefer to Lead Office of Administration
summary: Governor Mike Kehoe announced a major executive transition appointing Department of Natural Resources Director Kurt Schaefer as Commissioner of the Office of Administration, promoting Deputy Director Jake Buxton to head DNR.
seoTitle: Missouri Governor Taps Kurt Schaefer for Administration | Choseno
metaDescription: Missouri Governor Mike Kehoe appoints DNR Director Kurt Schaefer to head the Office of Administration with Jake Buxton promoted to DNR lead.
tweet: Missouri Governor Mike Kehoe appoints DNR Director Kurt Schaefer as Commissioner of the Office of Administration.
body:
Missouri Governor Mike Kehoe announced a significant restructuring of his cabinet leadership on Friday, appointing Department of Natural Resources (DNR) Director Kurt Schaefer to serve as the Commissioner of the Missouri Office of Administration. To fill the vacancy at the environmental and regulatory agency, Governor Kehoe named current DNR Deputy Director Jake Buxton as the new director, with the administrative transition officially taking effect on September 4, 2026.

The Office of Administration serves as the central operational hub for Missouri state government, overseeing statewide budget execution, procurement, state employee benefits, facilities management, and administrative information technology infrastructure. Schaefer, an attorney and former state senator who took the helm of the DNR in early 2025, will now lead the division responsible for implementing the governor's fiscal and operational directives across all executive branch agencies.

Jake Buxton's elevation to lead the Department of Natural Resources ensures continuity within an agency tasked with managing Missouri's state parks, safeguarding water and air quality standards, regulating mineral resources, and overseeing environmental permits for businesses and agricultural producers. Having served as deputy director, Buxton brings operational experience to the department's ongoing efforts to balance state economic development initiatives with environmental stewardship and natural disaster resilience planning.

The administrative realignment reflects Governor Kehoe's strategic focus on consolidating management oversight across core state functions. State lawmakers and civic stakeholders will observe the transition closely as the Office of Administration begins preparing initial agency budget guidelines and capital improvements recommendations for the upcoming legislative session in Jefferson City.
